integrity: The kernel norm is evaluated exactly as a Gauss hypergeometric function and normalized by Euler's transformation. The subcritical term follows from the connection formula, the supercritical term from the finite boundary derivative, and the critical logarithm from the zero-balanced derivative. High-precision calculations were used only as independent consistency checks.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns standard weighted Bergman kernels on the unit disk with fixed \(\alpha>-1\) and fixed \(1<p<\infty\). It gives the first boundary defect after the known leading Forelli--Rudin singularity and does not claim parameter-uniform remainders, general radial-weight analogues, or a quantitative essential-norm theorem for arbitrary operators.
title: Three-regime boundary defect of weighted Bergman kernel norms
